required_outcomes: Keeps the Monday 12 October 10:00-12:00 visit with Keystone Compliance: the verified tenant wants it to go ahead while she is at work, using the agency's spare key. No rebooking is needed.

Gets her consent in writing, as the key policy requires: emails (or texts) Clara on her details on file asking her to reply confirming the engineer may collect the office spare key and enter on Monday 12 October 10:00-12:00 without her there, and stating the visit stands.

Tells Keystone Compliance the tenant will be out, the visit is by agency key (collected from the office and returned the same day), subject to her written confirmation, and records the arrangement on R-5026.
acceptable_alternatives: Treating the recorded, verified call as consent and confirming the key arrangement to Clara in writing in the same message, if the message invites her to reply if she has changed her mind.
Rearranging to a day she can be in, only if Clara says so in reply.
positive_behaviours: Sets a follow-up for Monday morning to check her written reply before the key is released, and to confirm the key is returned (confirm_keys_returned) after the visit.
Mentions to Clara that she can withdraw the consent before the visit.
red_flags: Cancels or moves the Monday visit although the tenant asked for it to go ahead.
Arranges key access with no written trace of the tenant's consent.
prohibited_actions: Escalating a tenant-approved key access to a human.
Telling Clara she must be home on Monday.
critical_failures: Leaves Keystone expecting a tenant at home and Clara expecting key access, with neither told what will happen.
